originalTitle: Five takeaways from Canada's push to woo the world's richest investors
summary: A $1tn sales pitch, more than 160 projects on offer, pivot to the EU amid a bitter trade war with the US - takeaways from the first Canada Investment Summit.
content:
Canada's Mark Carney tells a story about Trump gifting him a key to the White House.

Prime Minister Mark Carney is pitching Canada as a "safe harbour" for some of the world's largest investors in an era of geopolitical and economic uncertainty.

Canada is "perfectly situated to build in the new global economic order", he told more than 100 major investors in Toronto.

The prime minister has pledged to bring in C$1tn ($720bn; £530bn) in investments in the ‌next ⁠five years as he seeks to reduce Canada's reliance on the US, and the summit he convened this week is a test of whether he can deliver on promises to strengthen economic resilience.

The stakes are high as the trade dispute with the US has pushed Canada to seek deeper economic partnerships with Europe, Asia and the Middle East.

Here are five takeaways from the summit on Tuesday.

Carney offers data centres and pipelines

Carney said over the weekend that the summit was chance for the deep-pocketed financiers attending, representing more than C$120tn of assets, to "come to 'peer into our shop window'".

More than 160 projects were on offer, from data centres to pipelines and port expansions.

Ottawa also dangled a series of new tax incentives, including a "mega deduction" measure in front of potential buyers, and the prime minister underscored government efforts to offer faster approvals for big projects.

Economic analysts have said Canada needs to make significant policy changes to help attract investment, including more competitive tax and regulatory systems, and ensuring a supply of skilled labour.

Carney said Ottawa will now offer "predictability" for major proposed projects, with the goals of a one-year review timeline.

"If we're going to say no, a quick no is necessary," he said.

On Monday, he held bilateral ‌meetings with chief executives from major finance companies, like BlackRock's Larry Fink and Blackstone president Jon Gray.

Airport privatisation ready for takeoff

One of the big announcements to come out of the summit was Carney's plan to allow private investment in four of Canada's main airports, in Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal and Calgary.

The prime minister said the plan would raise billions of dollars that could be reinvested in transport infrastructure, including smaller regional airports.

Many developed countries allow some degree of private investment in airports, but Canada has lagged behind and its airports operate through a not-for-profit governance model.

Under Carney's new proposal, the federal government will retain ownership of the underlying land and assets, but allow private investments into airport operations.

Labour unions have criticised the proposal, saying it will be bad for both workers and passengers.

"In the middle of a trade war, handing profitable public infrastructure over to private investors is exactly the wrong move," said Lily Chang, with the Canadian Labour Congress, in a statement.

But Nick Barry-Shaw, of the advocacy group Council of Canadians, said it was "a privatisation summit".

"This isn't ​nation building," he said. "This is country selling."

Canada is attractive for AI infrastructure

On Tuesday, the prime minister's office said the summit had generated nearly C$500bn in new investments across sectors like critical infrastructure, digital technology, energy and defence.

One sector that generated a lot of interest was AI infrastructure projects.

Canada has a cold climate, lots of space, and a "clean" energy grid, meaning there is space and capacity to build infrastructure like data centres, said Aidan Gomez, cofounder of AI firm Cohere.

Dave McKay, CEO of RBC, one of Canada's largest banks, told reporters there had been "a consistency of message" between the prime minister and executives, with all "pulling in the same direction".

UK in talks about joining global defence bank led by Canada

Carney's new love-in with EU has everything to do with Trump

Former Goldman Sachs executive and central bank chief Carney's political career was built in part on a promise to take a tough stance on the US.

After trade talks suddenly collapsed last month, the two countries have imposed tit-for-tat tariffs and been embroiled in a war of words. There are no signs formal trade talks will resume anytime soon.

On Tuesday, new US tariffs came into effect on a number of Canadian goods while some others were lifted, and bans on goods like alcohol and motorcycles are due to be imposed next week.

But the prime minister made clear the relationship wasn't over, addressing the American executives in Toronto directly.

"To our American friends, let me say this. We will always be neighbours, and Canada will continue to be the US's most important partner in many key areas," he said.

"After all, even at times of disagreement during our long history, we have always maintained deep ties."

Protestors on Monday accused the Carney government of selling off the country

Meanwhile, protestors accused the Carney government of organising a "great Canadian sell-off" of public resources and infrastructure to corporate interests, and hundreds appeared outside the opening night gala at a downtown museum.

"Half the buyers that he has invited here to Toronto are American," said Kai Nagata, with advocacy group Dogwood, on Monday.

"Let's be clear, every piece of our country that we sell off to American billionaires brings us closer to becoming the 51st state."

The prime minister heads to Europe next, where he will address the EU parliament and begin discussions "to build a unique security and economic alliance" with the bloc.

RBC's McKay said Canada will always be closely aligned with the US simply given its proximity, but there are opportunities overseas.

"I think this is an 'and'. We have to encourage our governments and encourage our leaders to look at opportunities to diversify trade and grow," he said.

chineseTitle: 加拿大吸引全球最富有投资者的五个要点
chineseSummary: 1 万亿美元的销售宣传，160 多个项目，在与美国激烈的贸易战中转向欧盟——首届加拿大投资峰会的要点。
chineseContent:
加拿大的马克·卡尼讲述了特朗普送给他一把白宫钥匙的故事。

在地缘政治和经济不确定的时代，加拿大总理马克·卡尼将加拿大视为世界上一些最大投资者的“安全港”。

他在多伦多对 100 多名主要投资者表示，加拿大“处于建立全球经济新秩序的完美位置”。

总理承诺在未来五年内引入 1 万亿加元（7200 亿美元；5300 亿英镑）的投资，以减少加拿大对美国的依赖，他本周召开的峰会是对他能否兑现增强经济弹性的承诺的考验。

由于与美国的贸易争端迫使加拿大寻求与欧洲、亚洲和中东建立更深层次的经济伙伴关系，因此风险很高。

以下是周二峰会的五个要点。

卡尼提供数据中心和管道

卡尼周末表示，此次峰会对于代表资产超过 120 万亿加元的财力雄厚的金融家来说是“来‘窥探我们的橱窗’”的机会。

共有 160 多个项目可供选择，从数据中心到管道和港口扩建。

渥太华还推出了一系列新的税收优惠措施，包括向潜在买家提供“巨额扣除”措施，总理还强调了政府为加快大型项目审批速度所做的努力。

经济分析师表示，加拿大需要做出重大政策改变以帮助吸引投资，包括更具竞争力的税收和监管体系，并确保熟练劳动力的供应。

卡尼表示，渥太华现在将为主要拟议项目提供“可预测性”，目标是一年的审查时间表。

“如果我们要说不，就必须尽快说不，”他说。

周一，他与贝莱德 (BlackRock) 的拉里·芬克 (Larry Fink) 和黑石 (Blackstone) 总裁乔恩·格雷 (Jon Gray) 等主要金融公司的首席执行官举行了双边会议。

机场私有化准备起飞

峰会发布的重大公告之一是卡尼计划允许私人投资加拿大四个主要机场，即多伦多、温哥华、蒙特利尔和卡尔加里。

总理表示，该计划将筹集数十亿美元，可再投资于交通基础设施，包括较小的支线机场。

许多发达国家允许一定程度的私人投资机场，但加拿大却落后了，其机场通过非营利治理模式运营。

根据卡尼的新提案，联邦政府将保留基础土地和资产的所有权，但允许私人投资进入机场运营。

工会批评了这一提议，称这对工人和乘客都不利。

加拿大劳工大会的莉莉·张在一份声明中表示：“在贸易战期间，将有利可图的公共基础设施移交给私人投资者是完全错误的举动。”

但倡导团体加拿大人理事会的尼克·巴里-肖表示，这是一次“私有化峰会”。

“这不是国家建设，”他说。 “这是乡村销售。”

加拿大对人工智能基础设施具有吸引力

周二，总理办公室表示，此次峰会为关键基础设施、数字技术、能源和国防等领域带来了近 5000 亿加元的新投资。

人工智能基础设施项目是引起人们广泛关注的一个领域。

人工智能公司 Cohere 联合创始人艾丹·戈麦斯 (Aidan Gomez) 表示，加拿大气候寒冷，空间广阔，拥有“清洁”能源网，这意味着有空间和能力建设数据中心等基础设施。

加拿大最大银行之一加拿大皇家银行首席执行官戴夫·麦凯告诉记者，总理和高管之间“信息一致”，所有人都“朝着同一个方向努力”。

英国正在讨论加入加拿大领导的全球国防银行

卡尼对欧盟的新恋情与特朗普息息相关

高盛前高管兼央行行长卡尼的政治生涯部分建立在对美国采取强硬立场的承诺之上。

上个月贸易谈判突然破裂后，两国针锋相对地征收关税，陷入口水战。没有迹象表明正式贸易谈判将很快恢复。

周二，美国对一些加拿大商品征收新关税，同时取消了其他一些商品，并对酒类和摩托车等商品实施禁令将于下周实施。

但总理明确表示，两国关系尚未结束，他直接向多伦多的美国高管发表讲话。

“对我们的美国朋友，让我这样说。我们将永远是邻居，加拿大将继续是美国在许多关键领域最重要的合作伙伴，”他说。

“毕竟，即使在我们漫长的历史中存在分歧的时候，我们也始终保持着深厚的联系。”

周一抗议者指责卡尼政府出卖国家

与此同时，抗议者指责卡尼政府为了企业利益而组织“加拿大大规模抛售”公共资源和基础设施，数百人出现在市中心一家博物馆的开幕晚会外。

“他邀请到多伦多的买家中有一半是美国人，”倡导组织 Dogwood 的 Kai Nagata 周一表示。

“让我们明确一点，我们向美国亿万富翁出售的每一片土地都让我们更接近成为第 51 个州。”

首相接下来将前往欧洲，在那里他将在欧盟议会发表讲话，并开始与欧盟讨论“建立独特的安全和经济联盟”。

加拿大皇家银行的麦凯表示，加拿大将始终与美国保持密切联系，因为两国地理位置相近，但海外也有机会。

“我认为这是一个‘和’。我们必须鼓励我们的政府和领导人寻找贸易多元化和增长的机会，”他说。
